observation.text: The speaker uses a critical and corrective tone while challenging traditional beliefs about sales techniques, describing them as outdated and ineffective.

citations.quote: The stage number one is unaware, where I literally do not have a problem.
Next stage is product aware. So understand this product or that product definitely going to help me.

observation.text: The speaker outlines the stages of buyer awareness in a step-by-step sequence from unaware to most aware, following a clear progression through these defined stages.

citations.quote: Authority is not the watch, the suit, the LinkedIn title. Authority is your inner position.

observation.text: The speaker dismantles misconceptions about authority in sales by juxtaposing superficial markers like watches and LinkedIn titles with the concept of inner position as an equal adult.

citations.quote: You're failing because you're trying to sell product to someone who is trying to solve a problem.

summary.text: Sales failure often occurs because one tries to sell a product to someone who is trying to solve a problem.

citations.quote: I learned it from twenty-six years on the phone, in the meeting, eleven of those in Dubai real estate.

summary.text: The speaker learned effective sales techniques from 26 years of experience, including 11 years in Dubai real estate.

citations.quote: my own coaching client make on average over one million a year in commission.

summary.text: The speaker's coaching clients make on average over one million a year in commission.

citations.quote: They are failing because they believe the wrong thing about sales. And the problem is not what you know. The problem is who you are when you sell.

summary.text: Many salespeople fail because they believe the wrong thing about sales; the problem lies in who they are when selling, not what they know.

citations.quote: Most sales people are working hard, but in the wrong direction, because they're chasing free outdated beliefs.

summary.text: Many salespeople work hard in the wrong direction because they follow outdated sales beliefs.

citations.quote: The idea that more knowledge, better technique, or the perfect closing line will fix everything.

summary.text: The belief that more knowledge, better technique, or the perfect closing line will lead to sales success is a misconception.

citations.quote: They're not magic spells. And when you try it, it doesn't work.

summary.text: Common assumed closing phrases used in sales, such as 'just finish the paperwork,' are not effective as they are not magic spells.

citations.quote: These sales gurus are already on a different level of authority. Their confidence is what they radiate.

summary.text: Sales gurus exhibit a different level of authority and confidence which influences their sales success, unlike regular salespeople who display the opposite traits.

citations.quote: He buys because he feels the pain of his problems and the need to solve them.

summary.text: Clients decide to buy because they feel the pain of their problems and need to solve them, not because of confidence or expensive watches.

citations.quote: And they often explain it through the magnetic word report. Build report and make them trust you.
But this is not how the trust works anymore.

summary.text: The traditional idea of building rapport to gain trust does not work with modern sophisticated buyers who recognize sales conversations as manipulation.

citations.quote: You just have to be more consistent.
Consistency without your sales system is just noise.

summary.text: Consistency in sales actions alone is insufficient without a proper sales system, as it results in mere noise rather than real progress.

knowledge.title: Consistency in Sales Is Not Enough

citations.quote: stage number one is unaware, where I literally do not have a problem.
moved to stage number two, the problem aware. So I do have a problem, but I don't know how to solve it.

steps.text: Stage 2: Problem Aware - Acknowledges a problem without a known solution.

citations.quote: Stage number three is when I'm solution aware. I understand that there is various solutions.

steps.text: Stage 3: Solution Aware - Identifies various solutions.

citations.quote: Next stage is product aware. So understand this product or that product definitely going to help me.

steps.text: Stage 4: Product Aware - Identifies helpful products.

citations.quote: The last stage number five is most aware.

steps.text: Stage 5: Most Aware - Approaches final buying decision.

citations.quote: Stay with me and you will understand why this is so important. So the stage number one is unaware, where I literally do not have a problem.
Next stage is product aware. So understand this product or that product definitely going to help me.

summary.text: Eugene Schwartz's system describes five stages of buyer awareness.

citations.quote: By the time the client comes to you, he doesn't need another salesperson to pitch and convince him. He already has all of the information.

summary.text: Modern buyers often do not require salespeople for information as they are already most aware and need salespeople for different reasons.

citations.quote: It's attention, authority, and need. Miss one of those and it doesn't matter how hard you follow up.

summary.text: Successful sales require attention, authority, and need; missing one results in failure regardless of follow-ups.

citations.quote: If you're usually saying something like this, Hi, it's Olga from XYZ company. uh you submitted your inquiry about ABC, how can I help you today? And it's over. The conversation is dead.

summary.text: A common mistake in sales is sounding generic right from the initial conversation, which loses client attention.

knowledge.title: Common Mistake in Initial Sales Conversation

summary.text: Authority in sales comes from an inner position of being an equal adult, not from material possessions or titles.
